title: Honest image quantification
objective: Identify and avoid common biases in image quantification.

steps.title: The threshold is a decision
steps.body: Counting 'positive' cells means picking a brightness **threshold** — and nudging it changes your result. In **[[Fiji]]** (ImageJ) it's one slider. If you set it while watching your groups' outcomes, you can unconsciously push the data your way.

visual.alt: Two simulated fluorescence images, control and treated, with the same spread of cell brightness. Cells above a brightness threshold are ringed and counted as positive. With one shared threshold the two percentages stay close; with a separate threshold per group, dragging one slider creates a large difference that isn't real.
visual.caption: Same cells, different thresholds: the 'effect' comes from the slider. Try one per group.

steps.prompt: What's the honest way to set a counting threshold?
options: Adjust it per image until the result looks right
Set one rule on blinded images, apply it to all
Set it on a treated image, then apply it to all
Set it separately for each group's brightness
steps.explanation: A fixed, pre-set rule applied blind to condition prevents the threshold from encoding your expectations.

variants.setup: You'll quantify % positive cells across two groups.
variants.prompt: How do you keep it honest?
options: Tune the threshold per image to taste
Blind the images and apply one fixed rule
variants.reveal: Blinding plus one consistent rule removes experimenter bias from the count.

steps.scenario: A figure shows cells 'brighter' in the treated group — but it was imaged at higher laser power and its brightness was stretched more in software.
options: Acquisition and display differ by group, so the comparison is invalid
Only the display stretch matters; laser power is a fair difference
Only the laser power matters; display stretch is just cosmetic
steps.explanation: To compare intensity, images must be acquired and displayed identically. Different settings make the 'difference' an artifact.
steps.followUp: Fix: identical acquisition settings, identical display scaling, and quantify raw values — not the stretched picture.

variants.prompt: To compare brightness across groups, you must…
options: Use identical acquisition and display settings
Match acquisition; display can differ by group
Match display; acquisition can differ by group
variants.explanation: Only matched settings make an intensity comparison valid.

steps.title: Rules that protect you
steps.body: Blind the analysis to condition, set thresholds before you look at outcomes, apply one pipeline to every image, and report raw measurements. These are the same **[[control|controls]]** and **[[blinding]]** ideas from C1 — applied to pixels.
